title: The 2009 Talk That Named the DevOps Movement
explainer: At the 2009 Velocity conference, Flickr engineers John Allspaw and Paul Hammond gave a talk titled '10+ Deploys Per Day: Dev and Ops Cooperation at Flickr,' arguing that developers and operations staff needed shared tooling, shared metrics, and a blame-free culture around failure rather than throwing code 'over the fence.' The talk is widely credited as the spark that led Patrick Debois, unable to attend, to organize the first 'DevOpsDays' conference later that year - giving the DevOps movement its name and its founding case study.

title: Conway's Law and Why Team Structure Leaks Into Architecture
explainer: In a 1968 Datamation article, 'How Do Committees Invent?', computer scientist Melvin Conway argued that any organization designing a system will produce a design that mirrors its own communication structure, because two components can only interface cleanly if the people building them actually talk to each other. For collaboration norms specifically, this is a caution: if dev and ops (or separate feature teams) don't communicate directly, the resulting software and pipelines will visibly show that same disconnect.
